content: The Dipsacales are an order of flowering plants that belong to the asterid group within the dicotyledons. According to the Cronquist system, this order traditionally included the families Adoxaceae, Caprifoliaceae, Dipsacaceae, and Valerianaceae. However, under the more recent Angiosperm Phylogeny Group (APG II) system, the classification of this order has been revised. While the general composition of the order remains similar, the families within it are now defined differently. In the APG II system, the order Dipsacales includes the family Adoxaceae and a broadly defined Caprifoliaceae. This expanded Caprifoliaceae family encompasses several groups that were previously considered separate families, such as Diervillaceae, Dipsacaceae, Linnaeaceae, Morinaceae, and Valerianaceae. Notable members of the Dipsacales order, as defined by APG II, include plants such as honeysuckle, elder, viburnum, and valerian. Additionally, there are a few other families that may be closely related to this order. These include the Columelliaceae, Paracryphiaceae, and Sphenostemonaceae families.
